decision: Reject this window as a positive relaxation lead: all four horizon means are negative before and after the fixed deduction, and remain negative excluding the largest path. This is a retrospective descriptive result, not a rejection of the approved HYPE strategy or a test of an executable replacement. Keep exact native-lifecycle collection as the highest-value investigation.
falsifier: A source-row or arithmetic discrepancy invalidates this numerical finding. Reopen the broader research question only with new non-overlapping observation windows or changed regime evidence, then preregister any executable rule and validate causal alignment, fees, funding, delay, depth and exits; do not retune thresholds on this sample.
hypothesis: The frozen initial V88 observation window supplies a positive descriptive lead for HYPE long annotations missing only the breakout-onset condition, measured at the existing 5/15/30/60-minute horizons after the existing fixed 13-bps deduction.
limitations: Non-overlapping windows are not necessarily statistically independent; all are from one session and horizons overlap each other.
The 13-bps deduction is a fixed diagnostic assumption, not measured execution fees, impact, funding or fills.
These are ineligible long-side annotations. Removing the onset condition also requires explicit alignment and execution feasibility; this is not an executable strategy backtest.
SOL annotations currently describe long source context despite a short-only executable route; they are not evidence of SOL-short returns.
No runtime or strategy changes are authorized by this report. First native lifecycle evidence remains outstanding.
The diagnostic uses selected episode-onset candle paths and omits a complete executable alignment, entry and exit strategy; it is not a live PnL estimate.
The negative window does not prove future absence of an edge and does not authorize a portfolio or risk change.

metrics.highest_value_next_investigation: HYPE exact-run native entry/protection/hold/exit fidelity and later execution repeatability.
